turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_shg_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format) and `shg` (the
    largest SHG tensor component |d_ij|, in pm/V).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, predict each candidate's largest SHG tensor
component |d_ij|, then select the 5 candidates whose |d_ij| is CLOSEST to 20
pm/V.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, closest first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
Using structural analogy to the training set, I focused on candidates whose POSCAR matches a training compound with a known SHG near 20 pm/V. The clearest cases are:

- `c087`: nearly identical structure to the training compound `Ca8 Cd4 P8` (20.26 pm/V), with As substituted on the P site.
- `c075`: same structure family as `Ga4 Cu2 Ag2 S8` (21.16 pm/V).
- `c097`: very close lattice/coordinate match to a `Li3 Mg2 Ga1 Se5` polymorph at 21.48 pm/V.
- `c051`: Zn analogue of `Cd2 Ga4 S8` (21.70 pm/V); Zn/Cd replacement is modest here.
- `c093`: Cu analogue of `Al4 Ag4 Se8` (15.61 pm/V), placing it nearer to 20 than most other candidates.

Final: c087, c075, c097, c051, c093
